[Previous context: Progress has been made in reducing] communicable diseases (MDG 6): the annual parasite incidence for malaria has been decreasing

consistently from 198 per 1,000 in 1990 to 16 per 1,000 in 2009, and the rate of confirmed

malaria deaths has declined from 32 per 100,000 population to less than 1 per 100,000 over the

same period (Government of Vanuatu Prime Minister's Department, 2010). The tuberculosis

treatment success rate is estimated to be 96 percent (WHO, 2012a). Despite relatively high

levels of sexually transmitted infections, prevalence of HIV and AIDS is currently very low: nine

confirmed cases of HIV and two deaths since 2002.

10. The Millennium Development Declaration was adopted by the United Nations in September 2000. It involved

[Context: 10. The Millennium Development Declaration was adopted by the United Nations in September 2000. It involved]
eight Millennium Development Goals including halving extreme poverty; reducing child deaths by two-thirds;
reducing maternal mortality by three-quarters; and halting and reversing the spread of major diseases between 1990

and 2015. Further details are available at http://www.un.org/millenniumgoals/bkgd.shtml.
